---
title: "Generate tracks"
---

Tracking uses [Trackastra](https://github.com/weigertlab/trackastra) (Weigert
lab, ECCV 2024), a track-by-detection model with pretrained weights and no
parameters to tune. Turn it on with `--track`:

```bash
uv run omero-screen 12345 --stitch --track            # default model general_2d
uv run omero-screen 12345 --stitch --track ctc        # another pretrained model
```

`--track` takes an optional model: a pretrained name or a checkpoint path. On
its own it uses `general_2d`.

## How it works

1. Tracking runs on the **stitched whole-well nucleus mask**, so it requires
   [`--stitch`](../user-guide/stitching.qmd) and follows cells across
   field boundaries.
2. Trackastra relabels the nucleus mask in place, so each nucleus's label *is*
   its `track_id`. Cell and cytoplasm measurements are tied to their nucleus by
   overlap, so they inherit the track ID.
3. Four columns go into the measurements: `track_id` and `parent_track_id`
   (curated) plus `track_id_raw` and `parent_track_id_raw` (unchanged tracker
   output). At a division, both daughters get new track IDs whose
   `parent_track_id` is the mother's.
4. On single-timepoint (fixed-cell) plates `--track` does nothing: the output is
   byte-identical to a run without it.

## Linking modes

Choose with `--track-mode`:

| Mode | |
|---|---|
| `greedy` (default) | Fast greedy linking with divisions |
| `greedy_nodiv` | Slightly faster, no divisions; rarely useful for cell-cycle work |
| `ilp` | Integer linear programming: most accurate and slowest. Needs the optional `motile` solver stack. |

## GPU memory

Trackastra's attention is a dense `(heads, N, N)` matrix whose memory grows with
`N²`, where `N ≈ window × detections per frame`. A dense well over a long
window can run out of GPU memory. By default this is handled for you:

- Tracking runs on the GPU and, from a calibrated estimate of the detections per
  window, **reduces the temporal window** until it fits in free VRAM. This is
  logged as `Auto-reduced temporal window X → Y`. A diagnostic line reports the
  number of frames, objects per frame, effective window and detections per
  window.
- `--track-window N` forces a window and skips the automatic fit.
- `--track-device cpu` runs the identical computation in host RAM. It is slower,
  but has no VRAM ceiling and keeps the full window: the choice when accuracy
  matters more than time on the densest wells. Without the option, CUDA is used
  when available, and CPU otherwise; Apple MPS falls back to CPU.
- `--track-batch-size N` (default 4) is the number of windows scored per forward
  pass. Lower it if you still hit CUDA out-of-memory errors.

## Correcting the first pass

Trackastra links detections; it cannot fix them. A nucleus that Cellpose
splits in two becomes a false division, and debris becomes a stationary track.
`--track-correct` corrects the first pass before anything is measured:

```bash
uv run omero-screen 12345 --stitch --track --track-correct
```

1. Every first-pass nucleus is measured, debris (stationary,
   reporter-negative tracks) is hidden, and the pieces of one split nucleus
   are given one label.
2. The corrected nuclei are tracked a second time with the same model and
   settings, so Trackastra sees one detection per nucleus.
3. The second pass is repaired too, so every division in the final lineage has
   passed the geminin test.
4. The corrected nuclei are measured: CellView gets **one row per real
   nucleus**, with every feature recomputed on the merged pieces.

The geminin test and the debris test need a PIP-FUCCI plate: a timelapse with
one channel named `pip` and one named `geminin`. On any other timelapse the
correction only merges the pieces of split nuclei.

The masks uploaded to OMERO stay the **first pass**. The correction is a table
over their labels, attached to each well as `track_correction.csv`
(`timepoint, label, track_id`, where 0 means hidden), `track_lineage.csv` (the
first-pass and final lineages, and which first-pass tracks were debris) and
`track_events.csv` (the repair decisions). Building the napari zarr cache copies
the table beside the cache, so the viewer shows the same nuclei that CellView
holds, as a `nuclei (corrected)` layer beside the first-pass nuclei. A rerun without `--track-correct`
removes the attachments, because they no longer match the new masks.

To correct an already-cached plate without rerunning the pipeline, use
`omero-screen-images correct PLATE_ID`, which computes the same correction from
the zarr cache.

## Tracks in CellView

Import the plate as usual:

```bash
uv run cellview import plate 12345
```

The track columns are picked up automatically, with no schema change, and can
be queried alongside intensities, areas and cell-cycle phase.

## Next

Open the well in the [Tracks widget](../napari/user-guide/tracks_widget.html)
to overlay tracks, inspect a lineage tree, export one track as CSV, or export
the well for [Mastodon](mastodon.qmd).
